findings.title: [P1] Restore removal of the socket message listener
findings.body: When a caller invokes the returned disposer, the registered handler remains active. Subsequent messages still invoke stale logic, and repeated attach/dispose cycles accumulate listeners and duplicate processing.

findings.title: [P1] Restore cancellation of the polling interval
findings.body: The interval handle is discarded and the returned disposer does nothing. Polling therefore continues after teardown, repeated start/stop cycles accumulate timers, and a live timer can prevent a Node.js process from exiting.

findings.title: [P1] Restore removal of the socket message listener
findings.body:
Calling the returned cleanup function no longer detaches `handler`. Any subsequent `"message"` after teardown still invokes stale logic, and repeated attach/cleanup cycles accumulate listeners.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore cancellation of the polling interval
findings.body:
Calling the returned cleanup function leaves the interval running indefinitely. `refresh` continues executing after teardown, and in Node.js the referenced interval can prevent the process from exiting.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore listener removal in the cleanup callback
findings.body:
Calling the returned disposer no longer detaches `handler`. Any later socket message invokes supposedly unsubscribed handlers, causing duplicate processing, stale state updates, and unbounded listener accumulation across reconnects or remounts.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Retain and clear the polling interval during cleanup
findings.body:
Calling the returned disposer leaves the interval active indefinitely. Polling continues after shutdown or unmount, repeats side effects, leaks resources, and in Node environments can prevent the process from exiting.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore socket listener removal on disposal
findings.body:
Calling the returned disposer no longer removes the message handler. Repeated attach/dispose cycles retain handlers and let an untrusted socket message invoke every stale handler, amplifying CPU/memory use and executing callbacks after their security/session context was revoked.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore interval cancellation when polling stops
findings.body:
Each call permanently installs a live interval because its handle is discarded and the returned stop function does nothing. Repeated start/stop cycles create unbounded callback amplification and resource retention; even one stopped poll continues privileged or network work and can prevent process shutdown.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore interval cancellation in the returned cleanup function
findings.body:
After `startPolling()` is disposed, the interval continues invoking `refresh`, retains its closure, and in Node keeps the process alive indefinitely. Repeated start/dispose cycles accumulate permanent timers and recurring work.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Detach the message listener during cleanup
findings.body:
Calling the returned disposer while the socket remains alive no longer removes `handler`. Repeated attach/dispose cycles retain handlers, duplicate message processing, grow memory usage, and can trigger listener-limit warnings.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
